title: Mosconi Cup 2026 Teams: Meet the USA and Europe Lineups
description: Meet the five-player Team USA and Team Europe lineups for the 2026 Mosconi Cup in Orlando, Nov 27-30, plus the captains, storylines and how to watch.
body:
Team USA or Team Europe? In just nine days, ten of the best nine-ball players on the planet walk into the Caribe Royale Resort in Orlando, Florida, for the 2026 Mosconi Cup. The teams are set, the captains are named, and one big question hangs over the table: can the Americans finally win it back at home?

Here is your quick, friendly guide to who is playing, what to watch for, and how to follow along from November 27-30.

Team USA: a mix of veterans and a returning hero

Captain Johan Ruijsink leads the Americans from the sidelines as a non-playing captain. His five-player squad is:

  • Shane Van Boening is the first American to qualify and is making a record 20th straight Mosconi Cup appearance.
  • Tyler Styer is a two-time Mosconi Cup winner.
  • Fedor Gorst is a former World Champion and former world number one, and he won the 2026 Reyes Cup.
  • Justin Bergman won the Cup in 2019 and returns after seven years away.
  • Skyler Woodward was the MVP in both 2018 and 2019 and has also captained the team in the past.

Team Europe: the champions with a six-year streak

Niels Feijen captains Europe as a non-playing captain. His lineup is full of big names:

  • Francisco Sánchez Ruiz was the first European to qualify. He is the reigning US Open champion and was the 2026 Reyes Cup MVP.
  • Joshua Filler is a six-time Mosconi Cup champion who won the 2026 UK Open and Reyes Cup.
  • Aleksa Pecelj had a breakout year with wins at the 2026 Phoenix Open and the Reyes Cup.
  • David Alcaide is a multi-time Mosconi Cup winner with World Pool Masters, European Open and Philippines Open titles.
  • Jayson Shaw is a multi-time winner and two-time MVP who captained Europe to wins in 2024 and 2025.

The storyline: can the USA end the drought?

Europe has won six Mosconi Cups in a row, from 2020 through 2025, most recently by 11-3 at Alexandra Palace in London last December. The Americans have not lifted the trophy since 2019. That makes this year a fun home-soil test: familiar American faces, a crowd in Florida, and a European squad chasing a seventh straight title.

Each team has five players. The top three in the rankings qualify automatically, and the other two spots come from wildcard picks. Not sure how the matches are scored? Our Mosconi Cup format explainer walks through the team format step by step.

What, when and where

  • When: Friday, November 27 through Monday, November 30, 2026. Play is expected to start around 1 PM ET each day.
  • Where: Caribe Royale Resort, Orlando, Florida.
  • Fan press conference: Thursday, November 26, 3:00-4:00 PM ET (doors open 2:30 PM), in the Palms III room at the Caribe Royale. It is open to fans.
  • Tickets: Available for all four days through the World Nineball Tour website.

How to watch

Coverage is expected on ESPN+ and WNT TV, according to the announcement from organizers. They also said more broadcast details are still to come, so check the official event pages close to the first day to confirm exactly where to tune in. We will keep our Mosconi Cup 2026 hub updated with times and daily results.

Three things to watch for

  1. Van Boening's record run. Twenty straight appearances is a remarkable streak, and he will want to add a trophy to it.
  2. The stars on both sides. Gorst for the USA and Filler for Europe both arrive with big 2026 titles, so any match involving them is worth setting a reminder for.
  3. The crowd. A home audience can lift a team or add pressure to every shot.

How to make it a fun event

The Mosconi Cup is made for sharing. Pool is a game people love to talk about, and a team event gives everyone a side to cheer for. A few easy ideas:

  • Host a mini watch party. Invite friends to your local pool hall or living room, and let everyone pick a team before the first match.
  • Add it to your calendar. Our Mosconi Cup hub has an add-to-calendar file for all four days so you do not miss the start.
  • Practice between matches. Watching the pros is the best motivation to head to the table. Pick a rack and try breaking the way they do, with control instead of brute force.
  • Keep a scorecard. Jot down each day's result and see whether your prediction holds up.

Whatever the final score, four days of top-level nine-ball in one place is a treat for any pool fan, new or experienced.

New to nine-ball?

Brush up on the basics before the first rack. Our nine-ball rules explainer covers push-outs, safeties and fouls, and the big tournaments page and Pro Events list show what else is coming up on the pro calendar.

So, who are you backing: the home team looking to end a long wait, or the European champions chasing seven in a row? Tell us in the comments on our Facebook page.
